products.title: Limited Edition: AHLEM X Jorden Bickham
products.body_html:
An acetate style with universal appeal, this sunglass innovates a classic pilot shape to express strength, versatility, individuality, and joy. 

Ahlem first crossed paths with New York-based stylist, creative director, and fashion editor Jorden Bickham in 2017, when Ahlem was a candidate for a CFDA prize.

Though their interaction was fleeting, it left an impression: Ahlem was struck by Jorden’s luminous calm and sense of purpose. Recalling that radiant energy years later as she prepared to launch the collaboration, Ahlem sensed that Jorden was someone to approach. As usual, intuition paid off. Over far-ranging conversations, the pair discovered a common language—including a shared interest in social and political justice. Both being congenital doers, it wasn’t long before a plan was formed: To pool their talents on a limited-run collaboration and donate the proceeds to an organization fighting systems of oppression and discrimination.

Each numbered piece is handcrafted by the artisans of Oyannax, France, in microbatches of 100 in Brownlight, 100 in Foglight, and 100 in Ashmilk. 

A longtime ally of the queer community, Jorden suggested the partnership benefit G.L.I.T.S (Gays and Lesbians Living in a Transgender Society), an NYC-based nonprofit providing TLGBQIA and BIPOC individuals with access to healthcare and housing services, among other basic human rights.

This limited edition style is final sale, no returns or exchange.

products.title: AHLEM x Palais Galliera
products.body_html:
AHLEM and PALAIS GALLIERA

The collaboration unites AHLEM’s modern, minimalist eyewear with the PALAIS GALLIERA’s world-class fashion archive, in a partnership of extraordinary style.

The Galliera is simultaneously casual and sophisticated, low-key and high-impact. Oversize, full-coverage lenses evoke the mystery, glamour and power associated with high fashion: these frames can shield the wearer from all intrusions, not just sunlight. AHLEM was also interested in conveying something subtler. The Galliera’s architecture—sculptural curves and softly inverted lenses—is plainspoken and unadorned, almost gentle. Minimalism is for the truly confident, because there’s nowhere to conceal poor craftsmanship or bad ideas.
